English: Open Table
A rough table or plank set out in the open, where the first traders gather with their goods. The beginnings of commerce for a wandering clan.
Barter Patch
A loosely organized patch of ground where barterers, peddlers, and hucksters gather. The market begins to attract more nomads and traders.
Traders Tent
A large tent at the center of the market, where itinerant Jewish merchants gather to exchange news and goods, and offer shelter to traveling traders.
Merchants Pavilion
An ornate pavilion of heavy cloth and timber, serving as a hub for trusted merchants and traveling moneychangers. Commerce flourishes.
Market Stand
A row of sturdy wooden stands, protected from wind and sun, where sellers can reliably display wares. The market becomes a regional focal point.
Exchange Room
A reinforced tent or timber structure where trusted brokers and Jewish moneylenders operate, enabling rapid exchange of currency and goods. Trade routes begin to converge here.
Market Hall
A grand wooden hall, decorated with banners and mezuzot, where merchants gather from afar. It boasts guarded storerooms and permanent stalls.
Guild Pavilion
A magnificent pavilion for the guilds of Jewish merchants and financiers, offering mediation for disputes and attracting elite traders from distant lands.
Grand Market Room
A fortified wooden structure with engraved doors, permanent offices for tax collectors, and a gathering place for the most influential traders and rabbis.
Jewish Grand Market
A legendary economic heart for all nomadic Jews, this sprawling market is known across the steppes. Its wealth and unity inspire all who gather within.
